summary: This work demonstrates repeated syndrome extraction cycles in a twisted toric code using tweezer-trapped $^{171}$Yb atoms, with mid-circuit measurement, qubit reloading from a MOT, and role-swapping to mitigate heating and loss. Up to 90 syndrome extraction cycles are performed with detector probability maintained at constant baseline $\approx 0.2$, and logical information outlasts physical qubit lifetimes of $\sim 10$ s by more than 200× when encoded in distance-7 repetition codes.
motivation: Repeated syndrome extraction at arbitrary depth is required for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but heating and atom loss in neutral-atom platforms degrade performance. Demonstrating stable, indefinitely repeatable error correction cycles is essential to validate neutral atoms as a competitive platform for quantum computing.
method: The system implements a zone-based $^{171}$Yb processor with 128-qubit capacity using movable tweezers for arbitrary connectivity. Twisted toric codes with parameters $[[16,1,(4,3)]]$ (det8) and $[[32,1,(6,4)]]$ (det16) are probed via loss-tolerant syndrome extraction with alternating data–ancilla role-swaps, mid-circuit measurement and reset (MCM), and mid-circuit reloading of a storage zone (SZ) from a MOT every 10 cycles. Minimum-weight perfect matching decoding uses loss-aware detector error models.
result: Z-type logical error rates without reload are $\epsilon_{\mathrm{cycle,det8}}^Z = 0.74 \pm 0.01\%$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{cycle,det16}}^Z = 0.56 \pm 0.01\%$, showing suppression factor $\Lambda_{\mathrm{no\ reload}}^Z = 1.9 \pm 0.1$ at 4 cycles. With SZ reloading, logical error rates plateau at $\epsilon_{\mathrm{cycle,det8}}^Z = 0.63 \pm 0.03\%$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{cycle,det16}}^Z = 0.64 \pm 0.04\%$ across 70–90 cycles, independent of code distance. Distance-7 repetition code memory persists for $\tau_L = 225(33)$ s, exceeding physical atom lifetimes of $15.6(5)$ s by $>10\times$.
